title: Modular Application Design
definition: A software design approach that decomposes an application into separate, interchangeable components or modules, each with a distinct functionality.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of it like building a car. Each part like the engine, wheels, and dashboard can be made or replaced independently, making it easier to build and maintain.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: In modular application design, each module serves a specific purpose and can be developed, tested, and updated independently. This leads to better maintainability, scalability, and allows for the reuse of components.
difficulty_levels.expert: Modular application design is a cornerstone of microservices architecture. By designing applications as a suite of small services, it becomes easier to scale and manage complex systems. Additionally, it supports the principle of separation of concerns, where each module handles a particular aspect of the functionality. This can lead to improved fault tolerance and performance.

extra_fields.insight: The conversation highlights the importance of modular design in building a scalable and maintainable software application.
